brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days (freeing ₹26.60 L cash for us) in exchange for a 5–6% price cut — their cash is stuck for 101 days, much longer than peers at 64 days, so they'll value fast payment.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 5–6% price cut if we pay in 15 days instead of 30.
priceAsk.target: A cut worth roughly half their borrowing cost of 12.16%, so about 6%.
priceAsk.basis: Their cash is stuck for 101 days versus 64 days for similar firms — cash is tight for them. They borrow money at about 12.16%, so paying 15 days faster (saving them half a month's interest) justifies a cut of about 6%. The market asking price for pharma sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg with ₹250/kg typical, and the verdict is MARKET-FAIR at the top of the fair band, so there's room to come down.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (down from 30 days) in exchange for the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹26.60 L cash for us, but we trade that for a bigger price saving over the year.

brief.financialLeverage: They are a ₹1064.86 Cr company, so our ₹6.47 Cr spend is only 0.61% of their revenue — we're a small customer, so we have limited muscle on volume alone. However, their cash is stuck for 101 days versus 64 days for peers, and they owe 1.25 times their own cash (₹282.62 Cr debt), so cash is tight and they borrow at 12.16%. They keep only 2.3% profit on every ₹100 they sell, close to the peer median of 2.5%, so there's very little margin to squeeze. The best lever is to offer faster payment for a price cut — cash today is worth their borrowing rate to them. Their credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable and they're in the grey zone for financial distress (Altman Z 2.36), plus they have EPF payment delays, so push firmly but don't squeeze so hard that supply wobbles.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They borrow money at a high rate
They owe a lot relative to their own cash
We are a very small customer to them
They already delay paying government dues

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film substrate and conversion — can second-source at scale.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter for pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source option (though their health score is D 31/100, so qualify carefully).

risks: Their financial health score is C (46/100) and they sit in the grey zone for distress (Altman Z 2.36) — push for better terms, but also line up a second source in case supply wobbles.
They flag EPF payment delays, a sign cash is already stretched — don't squeeze so hard on price that they can't deliver on time or quality.
We spend only 0.61% of their revenue, so we have little volume leverage — the payment-speed offer is our main bargaining chip.
Their profit is only 2.3% — a big price cut eats into that quickly, so frame the ask as a trade (faster cash for a smaller margin) rather than a straight discount.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help free up your cash by paying in 15 days instead of 30 — in return, we're looking for a 5–6% price reduction to reflect the value of that faster payment to you.
